title: Welcome to Your Virtual Private Cloud ☁️
description: Understand the VPC – your own logically isolated network inside AWS.

slides.title: What is a VPC? 🏢
slides.content:
# Your Personal Data Centre in the Cloud

A **Virtual Private Cloud (VPC)** is a logically isolated section of the AWS cloud where you can launch resources in a virtual network you define.

- You control IP address ranges, subnets, route tables, and network gateways.
- Resources inside a VPC can communicate with each other and the internet – but only how you allow.
- A VPC is **regional**; it spans all Availability Zones in that region.

**Analogy**: Think of a VPC as a fenced‑off plot of land inside a huge AWS data centre park. You build your own streets (subnets), gates (internet gateways), and security checkpoints (security groups) inside your fence.

quizData.question: A VPC is a ______ service.
quizData.explanation: A VPC lives in one AWS region but spans all Availability Zones in that region.

slides.title: The Default VPC – Already Waiting 🏠
slides.content:
# Every New Account Gets One

When you create an AWS account, a **default VPC** is automatically created in each region. It’s designed for quick starts:
- CIDR block: `172.31.0.0/16`
- One public subnet per Availability Zone.
- An Internet Gateway already attached.
- Default security group, main route table, and default NACL.

For learning, the default VPC is fine. For production, you’ll typically build your own custom VPC.

slides.title: Custom VPC: You’re the Architect 📐
slides.content:
# Design Your Own Network

A custom VPC lets you:
- Choose your own IP range (CIDR block).
- Create separate subnets for web, app, and database tiers.
- Control inbound/outbound traffic with precision.
- Keep sensitive resources completely isolated from the internet.

**Key components we’ll explore**:
- Subnets & CIDR
- Route tables
- Internet Gateway & NAT Gateway
- Security Groups & NACLs
- VPC Peering & Endpoints

slides.title: Pro Tip: Don’t Put Everything in Default 🚀
slides.content:
## Default is for Experimenting

The default VPC has a flat, open structure. For real applications, always create a custom VPC that separates public and private subnets. It’s a security fundamental.
